newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa '97 maize, sunflower estimates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa '97 maize, sunflower estimates unchanged.

text.p: South Africa's National Crop Estimates Committee said on Monday it estimated the 1997 commercial maize crop at 7.660 million tonnes, unchanged from its estimate a month ago.
This is sharply down on the 1996 crop of 9.694 million tonnes.
This year's crop was expected to comprise 4.139 million tonnes of white maize and 3.521 million tonnes of yellow, the committee said in its third official estimate for the new season.
Last year's maize crop comprised 5.836 million tonnes of white maize and 3.858 million tonnes of yellow.
The estimates committee's figures exclude maize grown in South Africa's former homeland areas which is mainly for subsistence use. This maize adds around 550,000 tonnes to the total estimate.
The third official sunflower seed estimate for 1997 forecast a crop of 450,000 tonnes, also unchanged from last month. This is also well down on last year's 755,000 tonnes.
